criteria.criterion: A new drain test (run with cargo test -p athena-cli drain) with an approved in-limit proposal and an urgent queued request works the urgent request first, and fails on the old behavior.
criteria.evidence: I ran `an_urgent_queued_request_is_worked_before_an_approved_in_limit_proposal` and it passed. With one job slot, the only run is `run urgent`, the stop reason is JobLimit and the proposal's job stays queued. With room for both, the urgent request runs first. I did not run the test against base, because I may not change git state. Why it would fail there, from reading the code: the old `drain_with` never asked `plan_entry` for jobs approved in the same pass, and the stub's queue plan holds only `urgent`. A job with no plan entry gets its own batch ahead of the planned ones, so the old code would run `job-of-...` first and the test's `worked == ["run urgent"]` check would fail.
commands: cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain -- approved_proposal urgent_queued_request fits_neither

criteria.criterion: A test shows the plan (Plan::build / the plan command path) lists an approved proposal at its ordered place by dependency, priority, rung, then age, defaulting to normal priority, with role or priority-record overrides honored.
criteria.evidence: `the_plan_lists_an_approved_proposal_in_its_ordered_place_with_priority_from_the_record_or_its_role` passed. It uses RealSteps and drain::plan, the `athena plan` path. The approved job defaults to normal and sits on the proposal's rung. The urgent request comes first, and the approved job comes before a newer normal request because it is older. A role `Priority: high` line makes it high. A priority record of low wins over the role and puts it last. In athena-core, `an_approved_proposal_is_ordered_among_other_items_by_dependency_priority_rung_then_age` (Plan::build) checks priority, then rung, then age, then the role and record overrides, then dependency over urgency. `an_approved_proposal_is_normal_unless_a_record_or_its_role_says_otherwise` checks the precedence. Both passed.
commands: cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain -- approved_proposal urgent_queued_request fits_neither

criteria.criterion: Drain no longer works approved proposals ahead of the plan; approved proposals are ordered by the same rules as other items and job-limit/budget handling still applies.
criteria.evidence: From the diff of drain.rs: every job approved in this pass now gets its plan entry from `steps.plan_entry` and is added to `view.plan`, and the plan is sorted back into age order. So `Plan::build` (in `prepare`) orders these jobs with the rest, instead of giving them a batch ahead of the plan. `RealSteps::entry_of` sets the priority through `plan::proposal_priority`. `approve_all` keeps its job-limit and budget check, and the stub tests `..._the_job_limit_holds` and `a_proposal_that_fits_neither_the_job_limit_nor_the_budget_...` passed. One leftover: if `plan_entry` returns None, the job still goes ahead of the plan, but drain now prints a note saying so.

findings.summary: An approved job with no plan entry is still worked ahead of the plan.
findings.evidence: When `steps.plan_entry` returns None (it does if reading the records or HEAD fails in RealSteps), the job is noted but left out of view.plan. The rule that unplanned items run first then puts it ahead of the urgent items. Drain prints a note when this happens, but the job is still worked first.

summary: The change passes: urgent queued requests are now worked before approved steward proposals. The cause was in drain. A job approved during the same drain got no plan entry, and drain always ran unplanned work first, so the proposal's job jumped ahead of the urgent requests. Now that job gets a plan entry and is ordered by the same rules as everything else: dependency, then priority, then rung, then age. Its priority is normal unless a priority record, the job's own words or the raising role's `Priority:` line says otherwise, and a priority record wins over the role. The job limit and budget still apply. I ran the four new drain tests and the two new plan tests; all six pass. One test, with a single job slot, runs only the urgent request and leaves the proposal's job queued. Another lists the approved job in its ordered place in `athena plan`, using the real records, and honors the role and priority-record overrides. I did not run the drain test against the old code, since I can't change git state. Reading the code, the old drain would have run the proposal's job first, so the test would fail there. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy (-D warnings) and full test suite (1475 tests) all passed, and CHANGELOG.md has a clear entry. Two minor findings: the new tests are in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs, which is not on the deliverables list, and if a just-approved job's plan entry can't be built, drain notes it but still runs that job first.
